purpose: Adds a dismissible post-activation welcome panel to the Dashboard tab guiding first-time users through 3 quick-start actions (page caching, JS/CSS minification, lazy loading), plus fixes a cache→cache_settings key mismatch across the PHP backend to align REST API writes with backend reads.
riskRationale: The feature is non-destructive (read-only panel with opt-in actions), all REST endpoints are properly permission-gated, and the cache key fix aligns with existing REST API usage. Remaining issues are CSS scoping, dead code cleanup, error handling in dismissal paths, and missing uninstall meta cleanup — none affect existing production functionality.

text: Well-structured PR with clean React component design and proper REST integration. The WelcomePanel uses declarative STEPS constants, per-user meta for dismissal, and correct error handling in the main step action path. However, 6 issues remain: the dismiss button hides before the API call completes, a global CSS override leaks .wppo-button--secondary styles plugin-wide, dead code from the old admin notice approach persists, the fire-and-forget dismiss_welcome swallows errors, and uninstall meta cleanup is incomplete.

reasoning: Two important issues must be fixed before merge: handleDismiss calls setVisible(false) before awaiting the API call (panel stays hidden on failure) and .wppo-button--secondary in _welcome.scss is unscoped, overriding base button styles globally. Four minor issues should also be addressed: dead code in class-activate.php and class-admin-notices.php, fire-and-forget dismiss_welcome in handleStepAction, and missing user meta cleanup in uninstall.php. All fixes are straightforward and safe.

message: Clean use of STEPS constant with per-step isEnabled() callback keeps the component declarative and easy to extend. Each step specifies its own tab, payload, and status check, keeping rendering logic generic.
handleStepAction correctly dismisses the panel only after API success (inside try block) and logs errors in catch without hiding the panel, so transient failures don't permanently block the user.
Enable buttons have proper disabled state tied to activatingStep, aria-labels via sprintf (e.g. 'Enable Page Caching'), and visual loading feedback ('Enabling…') — good accessibility and UX.

dismiss_welcome endpoint correctly uses user meta instead of plugin options for per-user dismissal state, and reuses the existing permission_callback pattern (manage_options + X-WP-Nonce) consistent with all other endpoints.

cache→cache_settings fix is consistently applied across class-main.php and class-abilities.php, fixing a pre-existing bug where the REST API update_settings and backend reads disagreed on the settings key.

handleDismiss calls setVisible(false) before awaiting the dismiss_welcome API call. If the API call fails, the panel stays hidden for the session but the server-side user meta was not updated — the panel reappears on next page load and the user cannot retry dismissing without refreshing.
suggestion: Move setVisible(false) inside the try block after the API call succeeds, and restore visibility in the catch block so users can retry on failure.

message: .wppo-button--secondary is defined at root scope in _welcome.scss, overriding the base button styles from _forms.scss globally. Because _welcome.scss is imported after _forms.scss in style.scss, the welcome-panel-specific styles replace the base styles for every .wppo-button--secondary across the entire plugin, causing styling regressions in FileOptimization, ObjectCache, PluginSetting, DatabaseCleanup, and other tabs.
suggestion: Scope the .wppo-button--secondary overrides within .wppo-welcome-panel so they only apply to the welcome panel's dismiss button.

message: update_user_meta call with get_current_user_id() during register_activation_hook never executes because no user session exists during plugin activation — get_current_user_id() returns 0. The welcome visibility correctly defaults to true via the absence of meta, but the dead code is misleading.
suggestion: Remove the dead code block (lines 79-81) since it never executes during activation.

message: The maybe_welcome_notice() method (lines 109-125) and its dismiss handler (lines 68-70) are dead code because the wppo_show_welcome_notice transient is no longer set anywhere — the old admin notice approach has been superseded by the React WelcomePanel.
suggestion: Remove the maybe_welcome_notice method, the welcome dismiss handler branch, and the render_notices() call to it (line 98).

message: The fire-and-forget dismiss_welcome call after a successful step action swallows errors silently via .catch(). If the dismiss API fails, the enabled feature persists but the panel reappears on next page load with all steps showing 'Active', which may confuse the user.
suggestion: Await dismiss_welcome inside the try block before hiding the panel, matching the pattern used in handleDismiss.

message: The uninstall script does not clean up wppo_welcome_dismissed user meta entries. The transient cleanup for wppo_show_welcome_notice is present, but the new user_meta-based dismissal flag persists after plugin removal, leaving orphaned metadata.
suggestion: Add delete_user_meta_by_key('wppo_welcome_dismissed') to wppo_cleanup_site() to remove orphaned user meta entries on uninstall.
